pairs.evidence: lib/claudeCli.ts:388 Every nested `claude` run (reasoning door and agent seam alike) inherits this process's whole environment minus four metered-auth variables, so the parent runtime's ambient CLAUDE* identifiers reach the child unscrubbed, and the reasoning door also runs without --safe-mode, so user-wide hooks fire from it as if it were the parent session.

techniques.evidence: lib/claudeCli.ts:161 The one spawn door strips a 4-name billing list, not the runtime's ambient identifier family (no CLAUDECODE/CLAUDE_CODE_* scrub anywhere in lib/); the agent seam adds --no-session-persistence, the reasoning door (cliArgs) does not.
lib/turns/ledger.ts:54 A turn whose owner died gets a first-class `orphaned` status, not `failed`, and the sweep never re-dispatches it.

lib/turns/runner.ts:257 The record is minted before dispatch and is the truth, and an engine answer that lands after a cancel is discarded rather than written. No model polling exists, so this is only a partial fit.
lib/agent/agentArgs.ts:36 The fence lives in argv built by host code. --restricted ignores the settings files the agent could write in its workspace, so the agent cannot rewrite its own policy.
lib/turns/runner.ts:275 When a kind's dispatch falls back to another rung, the record names the prompt that actually reached the serving engine, beside its receipt.
lib/turns/runner.ts:164 Turn kinds are registered by in-repo modules only. There is no operator- or service-tier code loading.
lib/turns/runner.ts:108 settle refuses by throwing, but every spec is team-owned, which is the technique's own 'when not to use'.
lib/claudeCli.ts:286 Each turn is a single headless shot. No mid-unit input channel exists.
